title: Getting around
description: Ask for directions, read a map, and find your way.

explanation.summary: Places and things take an article that says whether you mean a particular one or just the kind of thing. This unit is mostly vocabulary for asking your way, with the articles that go with it.

sections.heading: A particular one or any one
sections.body: The article el or la names a specific thing: el mapa, the map on the table. Without an article you are talking about the kind of thing, or about a place in general: vivo en Madrid, I live in Madrid, but trabajo en la tienda, I work in the shop, where the shop is one the listener knows.

examples.es: El mapa está en la mesa.
examples.en: The map is on the table.

sections.heading: Asking your way
sections.body: To ask where something is, use dónde está. To ask how to get somewhere, the useful phrase is cómo llego a, and the answer gives a direction: está a la derecha, it is on the right. Derecha and izquierda are feminine, because la dirección is feminine.

examples.en: How do I get to the market?

sections.heading: Near and far
sections.body: Cerca and lejos are adjectives, and they take the preposition de before a place: cerca de la estación, lejos del centro. They also work on their own: el mapa está cerca. As with the weather, the verb for distance is estar.

examples.es: El hotel está cerca de la estación.
examples.en: The hotel is near the station.

examples.es: El mercado está en el centro.
examples.en: The market is in the centre.

exercises.prompt: Pair each word with its translation.
exercises.note: Some places take de as well: en la tienda, en la calle, but a través de la ciudad.
Estar says where a thing is.
